title: SLO linked forecast and failure-mode playbook
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Purpose: create a lightweight, operational artifact that tightly links SLI targets and error-budget forecasts to concrete failure-mode runbooks and rollout gating criteria. The output will be an SLO Ledger + Forecast view and a templated 'failure-mode playbook' per service. Rationale: teams need a single, actionable view that shows not only current SLI health but a short-term probabilistic forecast (30-day window) and the precise steps and owners to trigger when the forecast shows imminent SLO exhaustion. This reduces ad-hoc firefighting and standardizes rollback/mitigation handoffs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype SLO Ledger dashboard that displays per-service SLI, target, and 30-day probabilistic error-budget forecast (P50/P90)
A failure-mode playbook template with clear triggers (forecast threshold and observed SLI), on-call contacts, mitigation actions, and rollback criteria for each service class
Rollout gating policy draft that defines auto-throttle and canary-hold thresholds tied to the forecast model for use in Console rollouts
One pilot service (runtime-ingest) onboarded with real telemetry to demonstrate forecast accuracy and playbook execution during a simulated degradation
Documentation page and one-sentence checklist for PMs/Eng/SREs to adopt the artifact within a release cadence

2026-04-12: Final docs and rollout checklist published
decisions: Use a 30-day probabilistic forecast (P50/P90) rather than deterministic run-rate to drive gating decisions — balances sensitivity and noise
Classify services into three risk tiers (core-runtime, secondary-platform, non-critical) with distinct forecast thresholds and playbook depths
Surface forecasts in Console SLO Ledger panel; gating rules will be persisted as config that Console evaluates during rollouts
Forecast model will initially use existing SLI time-series + simple exponential smoothing with anomaly damping; iterate to more advanced models after pilot
risks: Telemetry blindspots for private/on-prem customers could reduce forecast accuracy — mitigations: fallback to observed SLI and conservative gating thresholds
Teams may treat playbook templates as boilerplate and skip ownership details — mitigation: require owner assignment as part of onboarding checklist
False positives from noisy telemetry could block legitimate rollouts — mitigation: use multi-window confirmation (short-term + sustained) and manual override processes
Resource constraints on SRE to support pilot incident simulations — mitigation: schedule smaller scoped simulations and record learnings asynchronously
